I will be moving soon. Do you have experiences or advice regarding the moving process or how to furnish my new apartment?
From my experience, prepare for everything to suck.

Except for your furniture, put everything in boxes. If possible get all boxes of the same size for easier stacking.
If you are moving far it helps to pack yourself a nigh bag with one set of clothes, toothbrush, pajamas, and your ID and money, credit cards ect. This way you have everything you imidiately need and don't have to go through all your boxes to survive for a day or two
Where do you get so many boxes?

Most places that rent u-haul also sell boxes. Staples or office depot probably has them for sale as well. Linen and clothes could be transported in garbage bags, i would recommend buying the clear ones so it's easier to see whats inside and keep the black ones for actual garbage.
The hardware store or from a uhaul store.
If you have friends that work in grocery or restaurants those places get tons of boxes they toss out.
Liquor stores produce tons of boxes and are almost always glad to give them away free.

Just remember to label the boxes ....that missing kettle coffee sugar and mugs are the first things you want, and then the bedding?

Many a person has drank water from the tap because they forgot to label the boxes
Throw shit out, seriously, hauling unnecessary shit is a chore and you're better off moving light and re buying it.

We will throw a lot of stuff out, like our old bed. But the new apartment has no furniture, so we are taking some with us - we do not have money to comfortably buy all the new furniture for new apartment. We are also taking a washing machine for example.

Try not to do it all in one go either, it's very stressful. I moved in 3 weeks ago and the missus is due to give birth in a week, so I did most of the work. Also have a 50 hour week job.

Chip away and don't worry that stuff is still in boxes a while, especially if you're moving 2 houses into 1.

We will need a moving company helping us. We are moving 3 hours away, into an apartment without an elevator (elevator will be done in a year or two) and we do not have the car. But maybe we will start packing little by little.

Live without if you can. My first apartment I had my clothes, TV, and an air mattress. Bought essential kitchenware to start and slow pieced together other comforts. *Avoid the temptation to go into debt buying furnishings.

Label boxes with the rooms the contents originally came from. Make sure you tape the bottoms well if the contents are heavy. Rent a dolly from u haul if you don't own one. They are worth every penny. Uhaul also sells these straps used to lift heavy furniture. We still get use out of ours whenever we need to move something heavy like a china cabinet or my piano.
Get rid of the things you don't really need. Moving is a good time to sort through your stuff.

Warning, holy fucking wall-o-text Batman!

Ugh, moving is something with which I am WAY too familiar (wife was military for a few years). I have packed Everything and moved 10 times in 11 years.

Long ago we bought a few dozen 18gal Rubermaid containers to use as "boxes". With so many moves behind us now, that was Easily one of the smarter things we did. There is a downside in that it cost more for "entry" and you have to store the dang things. For a family who's filled 2,000sq/ft houses, this isn't really a big deal. There's always Somewhere they can be stacked to await the next move.

Past that, pack like with like.. meaning don't mix box contents. Full or partial, keep everything within a room, together (and labeled). I thought this was common sense till I helped a brother-in-law move. They just threw whatever was handy into any box. And obviously, Label those boxes (room). I tried doing a content list once, was more work than it was worth. Thought I will label the boxes with frequently used things (knives and cutting boards, for instance) to know those should be unpacked earlier rather than later.

Similarly, pack in stages. There's stuff you rarely use and that can be packed well ahead of move-day. Another one of those common-sense things my BiL blew out of the water. To take this further, you're most likely going to be packing over 2 days... or maybe not for a single person in an apartment. If you're spending "one last night", you want Everything packed but what you need the next morning. For us that's mattress on the floor, just the clothes we're going to wear, tooth stuff (having showered the night before and packed it away), and some food that requires no dishes (home made breakfast burritos popped in the oven is our norm).

Make a concerted effort to pack "rock bottom essentials", 1 spoon/fork/knife/plate/bowl/fry pan/etc... (this always included cleaning supplies for us, wife is a clean freak and has to clean before we unpack). You want to be able to know, beyond a shadow of a doubt where your food stuff and bathroom stuff is located. Maybe food stuff is less of an issue if you're good with eating out, we aren't (maybe twice a year, maybe once in 2 years).

You ARE going to purge some stuff with the move. Do that before you pack and move it (gah!, that dumbass BiL again, had family help him move a TON of shit he then threw away/donated instead of doing that BEFORE!), another one of those things I had previously thought was common sense. Anyway, you're going through everything you own anyway, might as well get rid of that thing that haven't looked at or touched in more than a year.

The only time we Ever bought something big/expensive was the first move after college/to the first job. When we arrived we had no living room furniture, dining table or washer/drier. We also had a few thousand dollars set aside for those things and bought them within days. We sold a bedroom suite before moving, but didn't rush to find a replacement after the move (kept the mattress/box spring).

It's a sucky experience, but sorta nice at the same time because you can purge, organize and "start clean".
Thank you for sharing all your experiences!

If you have the money, or your new job is paying for relocation, book a removal company. I did once, they came in, packed everything (they even wrapped the matchbox in paper before packing) and unpacked it all at the other end...to the point where I had to stop them unpacking my underwear and putting it 'gently' into the drawer. All I had to do was point.

But if you can't afford that luxury and it is a long haul, a company is also a good bet as they are insured so any damage on the way is paid for.

Short haul and/or skint hire a van and bribe a few mates (friends take more care with your stuff than the van man hired for the day) In either case pack the female underwear yourself lol.

To furnish....in the UK at least, auctions are the best . I got a silkwood wardrobe and chest of drawers both with bevelled edge mirrors for £36 whereas a mdf crappy wardrobe and drawers would have been over £100.

So if you have furniture sales and auctions near you (check the internet) you get real wood for far far less than new mdf rubbish as long as you don't want 'modern' furniture?
